newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish PM says vote for Sinn Fein is IRA vote.
newsitem.headline: Irish PM says vote for Sinn Fein is IRA vote.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton said on Wednesday that a vote for Sinn Fein in Britain's May 1 election would be a vote of political support for IRA "killings and murder".
Bruton said he had "lost patience" with Sinn Fein for its failure to secure a new ceasefire by the Irish Republican Army (IRA) allies in their war against British rule of Northern Ireland.
"A vote for Sinn Fein is a vote of political support for the IRA and the IRA's campaign of killings and murder," he told a news conference during talks with Northern Ireland peace broker John Hume.
He said Sinn Fein and the IRA "are part of one movement", adding that "a vote for them is a vote for the same strategy".
"All that killing does is make the problems worse," said Bruton.

Sinn Fein is contesting several Northern Ireland seats in the British elections and says that it may win up to three but will not occupy places in the British parliament because that would entail allegiance to London's sovereignty.

The party says it is contesting the election to demonstrate the depth of popular support for its policies, which say that Sinn Fein should be admitted to Belfast peace talks without preconditions by virtue of the party's public backing.
Bruton's words were also directed at Irish voters in elections due by November this year. Sinn Fein polls around four per cent of votes in Ireland and has no member of parliament.

Bruton, whose government is co-sponsor of the Belfast talks, said he had "lost patience with the (Irish) Republican movement's procrastination" and said the governments of Britain and the United States had too.

He condemned an IRA bomb hoax that wrecked Britain's Grand National Horse race at the weekend as well as a series of attacks attributed to the IRA's foes, pro-British Loyalists who want Northern Ireland to say British.
"Every act of violence is an act of equivocation," he said.
Bruton and the British government have refused talks with Sinn Fein since the IRA ended a 17-month ceasefire with an attack on London's Canary Wharf business complex.

Britain and Ireland and the United States say Sinn Fein can only be admitted to the Belfast talks, which resume on June 3, if the IRA gives up violence for good and makes a wholehearted commitment to democratic means to secure its ends.
Hume, leader of the Social Democratic and Labour party, was in Dublin to brief Bruton on the situation in Northern Ireland and his efforts to bring about a new IRA truce.
Hume dismissed media reports of an imminent IRA ceasefire and said he had "no evidence to suggest" that the guerrillas would restore a ceasefire they broke in February 1996.
Northern Ireland media reports say that the IRA is poised to call a truce to its war in Northern Ireland but will continue to strike targets on the British mainland.
